title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its plan to strengthen AI governance, focusing on safety, transparency, and accountability to meet the public standards raised in the Committee’s 2020 report. It proposes new regulations, oversight mechanisms, and collaborative frameworks with industry and civil society to ensure AI technologies are trustworthy and serve societal interests.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector. The policy aims to ensure that AI tools used in exams and assessments are fair, transparent and maintain the integrity of the certification process.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report investigates how AI systems use copyrighted works and evaluates the legal, economic, and social effects of this practice. It offers recommendations for policy makers to balance protecting creators’ rights with fostering AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, acknowledging the urgent need for action and outlining a strategy to strengthen AI regulation, safety, and innovation. The response commits to enhancing public trust, supporting industry development, and ensuring that AI systems comply with ethical and legal standards while fostering competitive growth in the UK.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the scope, objectives, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence influences public standards. It also includes a FAQ section to explain key terms, processes, and expected outcomes of the review.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence. The submission likely outlines the organization’s perspectives on AI policy, oversight, and ethical considerations.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how artificial intelligence is reshaping rules for medical products, making it clear that AI tools must meet safety, effectiveness, and ethical standards. It outlines steps to apply the AI White Paper principles—such as transparency, accountability, and risk management—to existing and future medical product regulations.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the world's most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑enabled defence force for its size. It outlines how AI will be developed, integrated, and governed to strengthen national security and operational capability.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness AI technologies for improved services and efficiencies while carefully addressing associated risks. It outlines strategies, best practices, and governance measures to ensure AI deployment is safe, ethical, and beneficial across the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report outlines how copyright works are currently used to train AI systems, detailing legal and practical developments under the Data (Use and Access) Act's Section 137. It highlights progress made, key challenges, and potential future directions for balancing copyright protection with AI innovation.
